description: Commit-time validation in the Svelte 5 data grid: a validator per column runs inside onCellValueChange, an invalid edit is rolled back with api.setCellValue to the previous value, the cell flashes red and the rejection is logged in a Recent rejections panel. This is the pattern for rules that must never let a bad value land in the row; for highlighting bad values without rolling them back, see the column validate hook.

faq.question: How do I reject an invalid edit?
faq.answer: Check the new value in onCellValueChange and, if it fails, call api.setCellValue(rowIndex, columnId, oldValue) to restore the previous value. The demo also flashes the cell and appends the reason to a rejections list.

faq.question: Is there a declarative alternative?
faq.answer: Yes. A column can carry a validate function that the grid runs for every rendered cell and paints failures red with the message as a tooltip. That flags bad data already in the source without rolling anything back; the cell validation demo shows it.

faq.question: Can the rules differ per column?
faq.answer: Yes. The demo keeps a map of column id to validator (email format, age range, salary bounds, a required name) and looks up the right one from the event's columnId.
